en.title: Fresh snow in the US Northeast compared: Bolton Valley Resort leads with 4 in in 72 hours (15 November)
en.description: The snow has pulled back since 13 November, from 6,880 sq mi (17,820 km²) to 6,039 sq mi (15,640 km²) today; for 18 November our forecast gives …
en.lede: The snow has pulled back since 13 November, from 6,880 sq mi (17,820 km²) to 6,039 sq mi (15,640 km²) today; for 18 November our forecast gives 382 sq mi (990 km²). Bolton Valley Resort picked up 4 in (10 cm) of fresh snow over the last 72 hours, 2 in (5 cm) of it in the last 24. That leaves about 3 in (8 cm) on its upper slopes, by our snow model. Field work in dry mountains teaches one thing: the map is a start, the slope itself has the last word.

p: Other resorts did well too: Mount Snow, Stowe and Stratton got 4 in (10 cm), 4 in (10 cm) and 4 in (10 cm) over the last 72 hours.
There is snow at 41 of 111 resorts in the US Northeast today, over 6,039 sq mi (15,640 km²) of ground in total.
On Tuesday 17 November the freezing level climbs to about 9,285 ft (2,830 m), above the top of the lifts at 3,117 ft (950 m): rain can fall even at the top.
Rain on fresh snow makes it heavy and, after a cold night, icy: the days after are better for groomed runs than for powder.
At about 2,336 ft (712 m), Bolton Valley Resort has 2 in (5 cm) today; a normal 15 November has 1 in (2 cm) there.
That is more than in 31 of the 46 past winters on this date.
In past winters the best snow at Bolton Valley Resort usually came mid-February / early March.
Day by day at Bolton Valley Resort: Sunday 15 November 2 in (5 cm); Monday 16 November 0 in (1 cm).

Height by height at Bolton Valley Resort: 1,558 ft (475 m) 0 in (1 cm) on the ground, 1 in (2 cm) more in the next 7 days; 2,336 ft (712 m) 2 in (6 cm) on the ground, 1 in (2 cm) more in the next 7 days; 3,117 ft (950 m) 3 in (7 cm) on the ground, 1 in (2 cm) more in the next 7 days.
From the base to the top of Bolton Valley Resort: 0 in (1 cm) at the base (1,558 ft / 475 m), 2 in (6 cm) at mid-mountain (2,336 ft / 712 m) and 3 in (7 cm) at the top (3,117 ft / 950 m).
On 17 November the freezing level at Bolton Valley Resort climbs to 0 ft (0 m) to 9,285 ft (2,830 m), higher than the top of the lifts (3,117 ft / 950 m): expect rain or wet snow on every slope.
Between now and 18 November we expect 0 in (1 cm) at Bolton Valley Resort and 0 in (1 cm) at Stowe.
Forecasts a few days ahead can change: look at the map again the day before you travel.

On 13 November, the Lake Pleasant 2.3 WSW station (1,778 ft / 542 m) measured 4 in (9 cm) on the ground, including 4 in (9 cm) of new snow in 24 hours. At the Shrewsbury 0.8 W station (1,486 ft / 453 m), the gauge showed 3 in (8 cm) of snow on the ground on 13 November, 3 in (8 cm) of it new in 24 hours. On 13 November, the Rome 4.8 SSE station (561 ft / 171 m) measured 2 in (5 cm) on the ground, including 2 in (5 cm) of new snow in 24 hours.
The resort numbers describe an area and come from our snow model; the stations measure one point only.
After fresh snow, wind builds drifts on sheltered slopes. Off-piste, the first days after a snowfall need the most care.

advice: Fresh snow has a short best-before time: the first hours. Early starts win.
South-facing slopes take the most sun and melt first; high, north-facing slopes keep their snow the longest.
Before you ski off-piste or go touring, read the official avalanche bulletin (links below).
Snow on the map does not mean a resort is open: check lifts and opening dates on the resort's website.
Get a powder alert in the SnowScope app to know when Bolton Valley Resort gets fresh snow.
